subject.title: fix(channels): keep healthy accounts running when credential files fail

question: Should OpenClaw adopt account-scoped degradation, rather than startup fallback, for every legacy channel account whose explicitly configured credential file is unavailable?
rationale: The implementation is broad and changes runtime availability and credential-precedence behavior across multiple bundled channels; real runtime proof and maintainer confirmation of the fail-closed upgrade contract are needed before merge.

options.title: Require runtime proof, then accept scoped degradation
options.body: Require a redacted live Gateway or terminal capture showing one unavailable account stays degraded while a valid sibling starts, then merge if the observed precedence matches the intended no-fallback contract.

options.title: Preserve fallback behavior
options.body: Revise the proposal to retain lower-precedence fallback for existing explicit-file setups if maintainers consider that behavior a required compatibility contract.

recommendation.title: Require runtime proof, then accept scoped degradation
recommendation.body: Require a redacted live Gateway or terminal capture showing one unavailable account stays degraded while a valid sibling starts, then merge if the observed precedence matches the intended no-fallback contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the paired report and the candidate implementation, so they are best positioned to provide the requested redacted runtime evidence and clarify the intended credential precedence.
